title: Compare M5 bottom-series forecasts on authorized competition data
summary: Actual-data verified for one recorded run on ten frozen bottom series (the first item per store) and three fixed 28-day origins of the official M5 validation-period sales. The four-week mean lowered unweighted MAE from 0.6774 to 0.6375 overall but was worse at the first origin; this is not WRMSSE or a leaderboard score.
split_definition: Frozen at most twelve bottom series; origins d_1829, d_1857 and d_1885; next 28 days validate; all forecasts/scales/weights use history through the origin.
metric: mean absolute error (unweighted; not M5 WRMSSE)
environment: Recorded with Python 3.12.13 and its standard library only on Darwin arm64, in one local CPU run on 2026-10-26 (about 71 s wall time; about 1.34 GB of traced Python allocations, which include input snapshots and full CSV parsing). Other Python versions and platforms are not covered by this receipt. Set private input/output environment variables as documented before execution.
steps: Inspect current M5 data access and rules, obtain authorized sales_train_validation.csv, calendar.csv and sell_prices.csv yourself, and keep them outside Git/public.
Freeze a private scope.json before running (the recorded run took the first item_id in file order for each store_id, with price availability unverified); never change it after seeing results.
Preserve origins 1829/1857/1885 and horizon 28; compare unchanged seasonal-naive and four-week averaging forecasts, then inspect every alias/origin diagnostic and retain worse and undefined cases.
Optionally compare a notebook run with the script run exactly; keep the private series map and forecast/error rows outside safe-review. No full-hierarchy score or submission.
limitations: One recorded run on one machine (Python 3.12.13, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-26); a notebook run of the same package matched it exactly but other environments are untested.
Only ten of the roughly 30,000 bottom series, chosen by a fixed first-item-per-store rule; results do not represent the full hierarchy.
The four-week mean lowered mean MAE (0.6375 versus 0.6774) and won at origins d_1857 and d_1885, but was worse at d_1829 (0.6232 versus 0.6000).
Unweighted MAE and optional bottom-slice RMSSE exclude full twelve-level official WRMSSE; this is not a leaderboard score and no submission was made.
Historical price publication timing is unverified, so no revenue-weighted diagnostic was computed.
Undefined scales, missing prices and zero revenue stay explicit without epsilon or silent exclusion.
Private series identifiers and sales/forecast rows are not public diagnostics.
Traced allocations are not RSS; the measured run covers only this bounded slice, not a learner compute budget.

project.outcome: Explain the same-method forecast comparison across frozen horizons and the limits of slice scoring.
prerequisites: Run local Python and configure private input/environment paths.
Explain forecast origins, 28-day horizons, MAE, scaled errors and revenue-weight limitations.

access.instructions: Inspect current M5 data/rules, supply authorized sales_train_validation.csv, calendar.csv, sell_prices.csv and private scope.json outside Git/public. Follow docs/m5-actual-data-setup.md. No automatic acquisition or submission.
access.authorization: Recorded run used the official, unmodified sales_train_validation.csv, calendar.csv and sell_prices.csv downloaded on 2026-10-26 through the Kaggle API by the repository owner's Kaggle account after accepting the competition rules, plus a private scope file frozen before any run. Readers must obtain their own copy: sign in, inspect and accept the current competition rules yourself, and download the official files; this site does not distribute them.

project.baseline: Repeat the last training week separately at each of the three fixed origins.
project.controlled_change: Compare the fixed average of four prior weeks on identical series, origins and 28-day horizons.
diagnostics: Do both methods differ consistently across all three frozen origins and selected bottom series?
Which slice RMSSE or revenue-weighted diagnostics are undefined, and what hierarchy/availability assumptions remain?

troubleshooting.symptom: Missing authorized data or access failure
troubleshooting.recovery: Stop before running: inspect the official data page and rules, accept them yourself if eligible, and obtain your own copy. The recorded receipt does not grant access.
Use the setup recovery table, restore pinned files and rerun into a new private output directory; never publish raw errors or inputs.
